scope: Bounded read-only scout of public GitHub, official Wunder RNN pages, and Denis Tomin's public LinkedIn post. No private Discord or other private sources accessed; no repositories cloned or executed.

galam_public_source_status.conclusion: No exact GALAM implementation or full technical report was located in the bounded public source search. Do not infer code equivalence from similarly named projects or from public challenge solutions.

author_github.tree_summary: Profile README, workflow files, and contribution SVG graphics; no GALAM model, training code, weights, or technical report in this repository tree.
bounded_github_searches: Repository search: GALAM Global Addressable Local Aligned Memory
Code search: exact phrase Global Addressable Local Aligned Memory
Code search: GALAM scoped to denisalpino
author_github.search_result: Only the profile repository was returned for denisalpino repository search; the two code searches returned no results. This is evidence from a bounded search, not proof that no unindexed or future source exists.

author_public_statement.type: Public author post; primary source for his own claims
claims_in_post: Names the architecture GALAM (Global Addressable Local Aligned Memory), describing it as combining Transformer, LSTM, and TCN strengths.
Describes temporal self-attention with a learnable relative-timestamp bias, a causal dual decoder using slow fusion, and a revised two-phase time-series ensemble.
Reports a consistent 7th place on public and private leaderboards, and says the GALAM-only model was the best public result when excluding ensembling.
author_public_statement.limits: The post does not provide model equations, source, hyperparameters, decoder layout, ensemble recipe, weights, or reproducible results. It says details cannot yet be disclosed and a comprehensive technical report may be prepared later. Its high-level description is not an implementation specification.
author_public_statement.placement_wording_caveat: The post opens with “I won” but later reports 7th place on both leaderboards; preserve both statements and do not convert either into independently verified contest placement.

galam_public_source_status.unverified_user_context: The task prompt supplied a Discord statement that source code/hyperparameters were lost with an SSD and that a rebuild scored 0.3839, followed by a four-model FiLM ensemble at 0.3871. This scout did not access or independently verify that private statement.

public_2025_wundernn_sources.readme_claims: Transformer sequence predictor with sinusoidal plus learnable positional embeddings, multi-head self-attention, and position-wise attention; 32 features; reported mean R2 0.396.
public_2025_wundernn_sources.evidence_caveat: Score and architecture details are author-reported in the README; this scout did not run or independently validate the notebook or weights. This is a public competing solution, not GALAM.

training_script.recorded_configuration: 32 input features; one-layer GRU with hidden size 128; window 256, stride 4; AdamW lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4; batch 64; 20 epochs; seed 42; sequence-grouped 80/20 split; train-only standardization; masked MSE excludes warm-up targets before step 100.

public_2025_wundernn_sources.evidence_caveat: README describes the 2025 task as 32-feature, 1000-step sequences and mean per-feature R2. The repository exposes a training script and weights, but no comparable public leaderboard result was established here. The trained GRU and the checked-in moving-average solution are distinct artifacts.

public_2025_wundernn_sources.reported_method: Causal GRU ensemble: 3 members at d_model 256 plus 2 at d_model 384; 32-feature input; masked full-sequence BPTT; sequence-grouped validation; equally averaged ensemble.
public_2025_wundernn_sources.reported_results: Technical report claims dev CV mean R2 0.3922, and cites public leaderboard #1 as 0.3920 and final winner as 0.3964. These are report claims, not independently checked official leaderboard records.
public_2025_wundernn_sources.evidence_caveat: Useful reproducible public comparison and report, but it is a separate GRU system and not evidence for GALAM.

version_guard.observation: The currently indexed official site describes a different task/version: the leader table is around 0.67; current submission docs describe 20,000-step sequences, 112 input features, and a two-value output. Do not compare those scores or code format directly with the 2025 32-feature, 1000-step challenge and GALAM reports.
